pleuritic and worsened when he sat forward
had not received a COVID-19 booster
sinus rhythm with benign early repolarization in the anterior leads
extensive patchy late gadolinium enhancement in a mid-wall to epicardial distribution

pleuritic and worsened when he sat forward

sinus rhythm with benign early repolarization in the anterior leads

concepts.why: The patient's symptoms of chest pain and diaphoresis, along with elevated troponin and C-reactive protein levels, and the presence of myocardial edema on T2-weighted imaging, are consistent with an inflammatory myocardial process, specifically myocarditis.

The patient's symptoms of intermittent, sharp, central chest pain with diaphoresis, and the presence of elevated troponin levels, are consistent with acute coronary syndrome, although the coronary angiogram was not performed.
The patient's symptoms of chest pain and the presence of mild systolic dysfunction on echocardiography and cardiac magnetic resonance imaging, are consistent with cardiomyopathy.

The patient's symptoms of pleuritic chest pain and the presence of elevated C-reactive protein levels, are consistent with pericarditis, although the pericardial enhancement was not seen on cardiac magnetic resonance imaging.

The patient's recent diagnosis of ulcerative colitis and the presence of mild systolic dysfunction on echocardiography and cardiac magnetic resonance imaging, are consistent with ulcerative colitis-associated cardiomyopathy.
The patient's symptoms of chest pain and the presence of myocardial edema on T2-weighted imaging, along with the presence of pericardial inflammation, are consistent with myopericarditis.
The patient's symptoms of chest pain and the presence of elevated troponin levels, are consistent with coronary artery disease, although the coronary angiogram was not performed.

The patient's symptoms of chest pain and the presence of mild systolic dysfunction on echocardiography and cardiac magnetic resonance imaging, along with the presence of myocardial edema, are consistent with cardiac sarcoidosis.

rationales.F01: Chest pain with diaphoresis suggests myocardial involvement.
rationales.F02: Pleuritic chest pain is common in pericarditis and myopericarditis.
rationales.F05: Ulcerative colitis is associated with an increased risk of cardiomyopathy.
rationales.F08: Elevated troponin levels indicate myocardial damage.
rationales.F11: Late gadolinium enhancement is consistent with myocardial inflammation.
rationales.F12: Myocardial edema is a sign of active inflammation.
